## TL;DR

<!-- Required: one simple sentence, as short as possible. -->

Design doc: <!-- Required before writing code and for every PR, including drafts.
Link the 1–3 page doc: GitHub issue > Notion > Linear issue, in preference order.
Cover the problem, approach, alternatives and trade-offs, and validation plan.
Include Related work and lessons: precise sources, relevant constraints, and
what the design adopts, adapts, or rejects—and why.
Use reply-summary presentation: leading TL;DR under 40 words.
Walls of text are forbidden; prefer visuals, tables, or short bullets.
Include a brief real example when helpful;
link supporting detail. -->

## Summary

<!-- Explain the problem, how the change works, and the result. Use bullets, a real
example, a table, call graph, sequence diagram, or short prose—whichever best
explains this PR to the reviewer.
Show the key steps or decisions that produce the result; listing files is not an explanation.
Check drafts and description edits too: does this explanation match the diff?
Headings other than TL;DR are optional. No diagram or source annotation is required.
Keep the whole body within 120 words, with no paragraph over 80 and no list
item over 40. No walls of text. -->

## Verification

<!-- Decisive command → observed result. Keep material risks, failures, and untested
behavior visible. Link detailed evidence; do not paste logs or file inventories.
For a fix, briefly report the observed failure with all production changes reverted
and the pass with the complete fix restored. -->
